caption: A stone from space that fell on Kansas, USA. It weighs about 320 kilograms. Gravity pulled it down to Earth.
credit: From Forest Ray Moulton, An Introduction to Astronomy (1906), page 313. public domain.

caption: The Moon. It is always falling towards Earth, but it moves sideways so fast that it keeps missing.
credit: From Forest Ray Moulton, An Introduction to Astronomy (1906), page 42. public domain.

caption: The paths of the four planets nearest the Sun. Gravity bends each path into a loop.
credit: From Forest Ray Moulton, An Introduction to Astronomy (1906), page 237. public domain.

caption: Isaac Newton, who worked out that the same pull makes an apple fall and keeps the Moon going round.
credit: From Forest Ray Moulton, An Introduction to Astronomy (1906), page 220. public domain.
